title: Single-object comparison for composite derived adjunctions
statement: Let a:L⊣S,p:U⊣R,b:K⊣T be additive adjunctions between abelian categories C,D,E, with L,S,U,K exact. Let a′:L_D⊣S_D,p′:U_D⊣RR,b′:K_D⊣RT be adjunctions whose counits have the ordinary single-object normalizations. For e:L⋙U≅K descend e by exact composition. Then inverse to the S single comparison followed by S_D of the R single-object augmentation and the derived right-adjoint comparison equals single of the ordinary right-adjoint comparison followed by the T single-object augmentation. Applying zeroth homology and the canonical augmentation isomorphisms identifies the derived comparison with the ordinary comparison. In particular this holds for the canonical derived adjunctions transported through the exact-left-functor identifications. The normalizedDerivedRightAdjointIso construction is exactly this canonical comparison and satisfies the composed derived counit identity.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, and compatibility of the Hom bijections with composition and localization.

proof.text: Compose the a′ and p′ normalized counit squares. Naturality of the a′ counit moves the R augmentation through it. The exact single comparisons form an isomorphism from the single of the composite left functor to its descended composite; their compatibility with e is the exact single-constants comparison. Apply the counit-compatible right-adjoint comparison square to the ordinary and derived composite adjunctions. All remaining associators have identity components.

Apply zeroth homology to the single-object comparison and use the canonical augmentation normalization for R after exact S and for T. Naturality of the single/homology isomorphism and cancellation give the ordinary right-adjoint comparison. For the named canonical construction use the canonical single counit formulas. Its derived counit identity follows directly from uniqueness of right adjoints and cancellation of the exact constants comparison.

theorem single_adjunction_comparison
    {C D E : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] [Category E]
    [Abelian C] [Abelian D] [Abelian E]
    [HasDerivedCategory C] [HasDerivedCategory D] [HasDerivedCategory E]
    [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions E]
    {L : C ⥤ D} {S : D ⥤ C} {U : D ⥤ E} {R : E ⥤ D}
    {K : C ⥤ E} {T : E ⥤ C}
    [L.Additive] [S.Additive] [U.Additive] [R.Additive] [K.Additive] [T.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits L] [PreservesFiniteColimits L]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits S] [PreservesFiniteColimits S]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits U] [PreservesFiniteColimits U]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits K] [PreservesFiniteColimits K]
    (a : L ⊣ S) (p : U ⊣ R) (b : K ⊣ T)
    (a' : L.mapDerivedCategory ⊣ S.mapDerivedCategory)
    (p' : U.mapDerivedCategory ⊣ R.rightDerivedFunctor)
    (b' : K.mapDerivedCategory ⊣ T.rightDerivedFunctor)
    (ha : ∀ X, L.mapDerivedCategory.map
        ((S.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).inv.app X) ≫
      a'.counit.app ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor D 0).obj X) =
        (L.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app (S.obj X) ≫
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor D 0).map (a.counit.app X))
    (hp : ∀ X, U.mapDerivedCategory.map (R.singleRightDerivedUnit.app X) ≫
      p'.counit.app ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor E 0).obj X) =
        (U.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app (R.obj X) ≫
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor E 0).map (p.counit.app X))
    (hb : ∀ X, K.mapDerivedCategory.map (T.singleRightDerivedUnit.app X) ≫
      b'.counit.app ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor E 0).obj X) =
        (K.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app (T.obj X) ≫
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor E 0).map (b.counit.app X))
    (e : L ⋙ U ≅ K) (X : E) :
    (S.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).inv.app (R.obj X) ≫
      S.mapDerivedCategory.map (R.singleRightDerivedUnit.app X) ≫
      (((a'.comp p').ofNatIsoLeft
        ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso L U).symm ≪≫
          Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso e)).rightAdjointUniq b').hom.app
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor E 0).obj X) =
    (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor C 0).map
      ((((a.comp p).ofNatIsoLeft e).rightAdjointUniq b).hom.app X) ≫
        T.singleRightDerivedUnit.app X
